correctness.rationale: PASS — On C_n (n≥5), a graph-Lipschitz potential corresponds exactly to mean-zero edge gradients g_j of magnitude ≤1. ℓ1/ℓ∞ duality makes norm equal min_c Σ|p_t(j)−c|. For t>0, radial heat differences solve irreducible Metzler tridiagonal ODE with positive initial first coordinate, so p_t(0)>p_t(1)>...>p_t(⌊n/2⌋). Counting radial multiplicities proves the same median p_t(k), k=⌊(n+2)/4⌋, for all t. The stated zero-sum gradient g=1,(n−4k)/2,−1 is a simultaneous extremizer. Unique shortest k-walk gives p_t(k)=t^k/k!+O_n(t^(k+1)), hence leading defect (4k+2−n)/k!, positive for each residue class n mod 4. Positivity and semigroup norm submultiplicativity give strict all-time decay; t=0 and fixed-n asymptotic handled. Independently checked 24 LP norms against median and 11 exact Taylor coefficients, not as proof of infinite n.
